# 100mini — full context

Source: https://100mini.com
Last updated: 2026-10

100mini is instant single-file HTML hosting with no signup. You paste AI-generated
HTML (Claude artifacts, ChatGPT Canvas, v0, any LLM) or upload one .html/.zip file
and get a live, shareable link in about 30 seconds — no repository, build, or
server. Anonymous uploads auto-destroy after 7 days; a free account keeps 5 pages
permanently, and logged-in users can also set an expiry, cap the number of views,
or create a one-time burn-after-reading link. It is aimed at non-technical
creators who just produced HTML with an AI tool and need to preview, host, or
share it — without setting up Git, a build, or a hosting account.

## How to publish a page
1. Prepare HTML with an AI tool or an editor (single-file HTML, or a .zip with index.html).
2. Paste the code or upload the file; optionally add a title, category and tags.
3. Publish and copy the shareable link (or the QR code). It opens full-screen on any device.

## How to host a single HTML file
1. Paste a self-contained .html file, or upload one .html or a .zip that contains index.html at its root.
2. Click Publish — there is no repository, commit, build step, or server to configure.
3. Copy the URL or QR code; the page opens full-screen on any device.
This is the fastest path for sharing an interactive prototype, a client demo, or a one-page tool without GitHub or a hosting account. See https://100mini.com/host-single-html.

## How to publish a Claude artifact as a live link
1. In Claude, click the copy button on any HTML artifact (top-right of the code block).
2. Paste the HTML into https://100mini.com/claude-artifact-to-link and click Publish.
3. You get a shareable, full-screen live link in seconds — no downloads or local server.

## How to create a temporary (expiring) HTML link
1. Paste a self-contained .html file, or upload one .html or a .zip that contains index.html.
2. Log in and choose an expiry: 1 hour, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, or a custom duration (1 minute–30 days); optionally cap the number of views.
3. Publish and copy the URL or QR code. When the timer ends — or the view cap is reached — the page is deleted automatically.
Anonymous pages expire after 7 days by default, so no-account users get a temporary link out of the box. See https://100mini.com/temporary-link.

## Expiring and one-time (burn-after-reading) links
Logged-in users can control a page's lifetime in the publish panel. All of these
options are free — they do not cost in-app points and do not consume the free
permanent-page quota:
- Expiry: 1 hour, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, or a custom duration (1 minute–30 days).
- Max views: 1, 3, 5, 10, or unlimited. When the limit is reached the page burns.
- One-time link: a burn-after-reading link (max views = 1). The link opens once,
  then the content is deleted from the server and only a playful "turned to
  digital ashes" notice remains.
Crawler and link-preview requests (bots, prefetch/preview headers) are not counted
as views, so a one-time link is not burned by an instant-messaging preview.
Expiring and one-time pages are excluded from the Learning Square.

## Free tools
- Claude to Link (https://100mini.com/claude-artifact-to-link): paste a Claude artifact, get a live link.
- Single-file HTML hosting (https://100mini.com/host-single-html): paste one .html, get a shareable link — no Git or build.
- Temporary link (https://100mini.com/temporary-link): host a page that expires on a timer, optionally with a view cap.
- Markdown to HTML (https://100mini.com/md2html): render Markdown with 9 brand templates.
- Any to Markdown (https://100mini.com/any2md): convert Word/PPT/Excel/PDF to Markdown locally.
- ID photo (https://100mini.com/idphoto): AI background removal for 24 compliant ID photo sizes.
- Pomodoro (https://100mini.com/pomodoro), Rhythm (https://100mini.com/rhythm): focus and music tools.
- All tools: https://100mini.com/freetool

## Comparisons
100mini is often evaluated against other ways to put HTML online. A comparison hub
lives at https://100mini.com/alternatives.
- 100mini vs Netlify Drop (https://100mini.com/alternatives/netlify-drop): Netlify Drop is a doorway to the full Netlify platform (builds, functions, custom domains, free tier with 300 credits/month). 100mini is narrower and aimed at non-technical creators: one static HTML file, no account, live link in ~30s, expiry/view limits and one-time burn-after-reading links, optional share to the Learning Square gallery, and anonymous pages that auto-destroy after 7 days. Use Netlify for apps with a build step; use 100mini to share one AI-generated file fast without Git or a build.
- 100mini vs Tiiny Host (https://100mini.com/alternatives/tiiny-host): Tiiny Host is simple static hosting, but the free plan needs an account, caps uploads at 3 MB, adds a banner, and links lapse without periodic logins. 100mini is no-account and no-banner, with expiry, view limits, and one-time burn links.
- 100mini vs CodePen (https://100mini.com/alternatives/codepen): CodePen is an editor-first, public-by-default playground (privacy needs a paid plan). 100mini hosts a finished, full-page HTML file with no editor and no public feed unless you opt in to the Learning Square gallery.
- 100mini vs Vercel (https://100mini.com/alternatives/vercel): Vercel is a frontend cloud for real apps (Git, builds, functions, previews) and its free Hobby plan is non-commercial only. 100mini is a no-account, no-deploy link for one finished HTML file.
- 100mini vs GitHub Pages (https://100mini.com/alternatives/github-pages): GitHub Pages requires a repository and Git, and its terms restrict commercial use. 100mini needs no repository or Git and adds expiry, view limits, and one-time burn links.
- 100mini vs Claude artifacts / ChatGPT Canvas (https://100mini.com/alternatives/ai-native-share): in-chat sharing is one click but runs in the AI platform's sandbox, shows an "unverified" label, and may not be public. 100mini turns the same HTML into a portable, full-page link that opens anywhere.
- Note: 100mini offers a custom link path (/p/your-name, 10 in-app points) but not a custom domain.

## Limits and pricing
See https://100mini.com/pricing.md. Summary: anonymous is free (5 MB, 7-day
expiry); a free account has 5 permanent pages and 50 starting points; larger
files, extra pages, and custom links use points; membership (unlimited permanent
pages, no quota fee) is granted by the team. Expiry, view limits, and one-time
burn-after-reading links are always free and do not consume the permanent-page quota.

## Safety
Every hosted page runs in a Content-Security-Policy sandbox and shows a
phishing-protection banner. Code runs client-side only. When a page expires or is
burned its content is deleted from storage; a minimal metadata record (no page
content) may be retained for abuse prevention. Anonymous pages are excluded from
search engines (noindex).

## Frequently asked questions
Q: How do I instantly host AI-generated HTML without signing up?
A: Paste your code into the text area or upload a .html/.zip file, then click Publish. You get a shareable link in about 30 seconds. No account required — anonymous uploads auto-destroy after 7 days.

Q: Where can I paste raw HTML code to get a live, public link?
A: Use the "Paste Code" tab on https://100mini.com. Paste your HTML/CSS/JS, click Publish, and get a full-screen shareable link instantly.

Q: What's the fastest free way to publish a single-file web prototype?
A: Zero configuration: no CLI, no DNS setup, no server needed. Paste your code or drag-drop a file and it goes live in under 15 seconds.

Q: What file formats and sizes are supported?
A: .html, .htm, and .zip files up to 5 MB. ZIP archives must contain an index.html as the entry point.

Q: How long do my pages stay online?
A: Anonymous uploads auto-destroy after 7 days. Logged-in users get 5 permanent slots free; they can also set an expiry (1 hour–30 days), cap views (1/3/5/10/∞), or make a one-time burn-after-reading link. Members have unlimited permanent storage.

Q: How do I make a link that can only be opened once (burn after reading)?
A: Log in, and in the publish panel choose "One-time link · burn after opening". The link opens once, then its content is deleted and only a playful digital-ashes notice remains. You can also set an expiry or a view limit instead. It is free.

Q: How do I turn an AI prompt output into a playable web URL for friends?
A: Copy the HTML from Claude, ChatGPT, or any AI tool, paste it into 100mini, and click Publish. You get a mobile-friendly shareable link instantly.

Q: Is this a safe host for LLM artifacts and interactive UI mockups?
A: Every page gets a Content-Security-Policy sandbox and a security banner to prevent phishing. No data is retained after expiry. All code runs client-side only.

Q: Can I share my page on social media with a preview card?
A: Yes. Log in and check "Share to Square" when publishing. Links include Open Graph metadata for rich previews.

Q: How do I publish a Claude artifact as a live webpage?
A: In Claude, click the copy button on any HTML artifact. Paste the code into 100mini's "Paste Code" tab and click Publish. Your artifact becomes a shareable, full-screen live page in seconds.
